title: Environment & Climate — UNEP, UNFCCC, IPCC, Green Climate Fund
shortDescription: The organization that runs environmental policy, the treaty framework it sits inside, and the science body that isn't an organization at all.
genZNote: One org, one treaty framework, one science panel, one fund — memorise which is which and traps mostly disappear.

sections.heading: UNEP — United Nations Environment Programme
bullets: Established: 1972, following the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment (the first major global environment summit).
Headquarters: Nairobi, Kenya — the only major UN body headquartered in a developing country / the Global South.
A UN PROGRAMME (created by GA resolution, funded via the UN system), not a specialized agency — coordinates the UN's environmental activities and helps develop international environmental policy.

sections.heading: UNFCCC — UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
bullets: A TREATY, not an organization — adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, entered into force 1994.
It created the annual 'Conference of the Parties' (COP) meetings — COP is the treaty's governing/decision-making event, not a separate body.

Two major agreements were negotiated under the UNFCCC umbrella: the Kyoto Protocol (1997, binding emissions targets for developed countries) and the Paris Agreement (2015, adopted at COP21, nationally determined contributions for all parties).
The UNFCCC Secretariat is headquartered in Bonn, Germany.

sections.heading: IPCC — Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
bullets: Established: 1988, jointly by UNEP and WMO (World Meteorological Organization) — a scientific ASSESSMENT BODY, not a policy-making or treaty organization.
Headquartered administratively at WMO's Geneva offices (it has no independent standalone HQ building in the way a full organization does).
Its job: synthesize and assess climate science for policymakers through periodic 'Assessment Reports' — it does not itself set targets or negotiate agreements; that's the UNFCCC/COP's job.
Shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.

sections.heading: Green Climate Fund (GCF)
bullets: Established: 2010, under the UNFCCC framework, to help developing countries with climate mitigation/adaptation financing.
Distinct from the IPCC (science) and UNFCCC (treaty framework) — the GCF is specifically the FINANCING mechanism.

columnHeaders: What kind of thing is it?
rows: Scientific assessment body — no policy authority

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: UNEP is the UN's environment programme (1972, Nairobi); the UNFCCC is the 1992 treaty that created the COP process; the IPCC is the UNEP/WMO scientific assessment body (1988); the Green Climate Fund is the UNFCCC's financing arm (2010).
keyFacts: UNEP: 1972, HQ Nairobi — the only major UN body HQ'd in the developing world.
UNFCCC: treaty, adopted 1992 (Rio), in force 1994; Secretariat in Bonn; created the COP.
IPCC: 1988, jointly by UNEP + WMO — assesses science, does not set policy.
Kyoto Protocol (1997) and Paris Agreement (2015, COP21) were both negotiated under UNFCCC.
Green Climate Fund: 2010, HQ Songdo, South Korea.
commonConfusion: UNFCCC is a TREATY; UNEP is an ORGANIZATION — don't call UNFCCC an 'agency'.
IPCC does not negotiate or set emissions targets — that happens at COP under the UNFCCC; IPCC only assesses the science.

highYieldFacts: UNEP HQ is Nairobi — the only major UN body headquartered in the Global South.
IPCC was jointly established by UNEP and WMO in 1988.
Paris Agreement adopted at COP21 (2015); Kyoto Protocol adopted 1997 — both under the UNFCCC.
commonTraps: Do not confuse the IPCC (science) with the UNFCCC (treaty/negotiation framework) — a very frequently tested distinction.
COP is not a separate organization — it is the UNFCCC's own governing conference.
mustRemember: UNEP est. 1972 after the Stockholm Conference. UNFCCC adopted 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit.
Green Climate Fund is the financing mechanism, separate from the science (IPCC) and the treaty (UNFCCC).

confusedTerms.distinction: UNFCCC is the binding treaty framework under which countries negotiate climate commitments (via COP); IPCC is a scientific body that assesses climate research and has no negotiating or policy-setting role.

possibleQuestions: Which two bodies jointly established the IPCC, and in which year?
Where is the UNEP headquartered, and why is that fact often highlighted?
